## About these sources

Mumbai only. The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation has 227
ward seats; two councils are in the schema, `ulb_ward_2012` and `ulb_ward_2017`.

The original research collection under `raw/mumbai/` supplied result tables,
with reservations stated in the "Present Reservation" column of
`BMC-2007_raw.xlsx`. **That column is the 2012 draw, not 2007's.** It lists 115
women's seats where the 2007 council had 76 (one third), and it agrees ward for
ward with the deposit's 2012-term flag on 226 of 227 wards. The remaining ward,
172, is now corrected from SC Women to SC using the official bilingual BMC ward
description (`raw/mumbai/source_review/f_north_2012.pdf`, PDF page 17). The
reviewed release has 114 women-reserved seats and agrees with all 227 deposit
flags. The original sheet and a row-level correction ledger are retained.
Its "Sitting Corporator" column holds the 2007 winners. So the sheet supplies
the 2012 slice's reservation and the 2007 supplemental file's winners.

The 2017 slice takes its reservation from the replication deposit for
Karekurve-Ramachandra & Lee (2025, *Comparative Political Studies*), Harvard
Dataverse doi:10.7910/DVN/IO9SLQ, CC0, held under `raw/mumbai/dataverse_IO9SLQ/`
with a manifest and checksums. The authors digitised the commission's result
handbooks, so for 2017 the reservation is a secondary source. Winners for 2012
come from a scan transcription (202 of 227 wards named; names are surname-first
and phonetic) and for 2017 from the commission's result export; both are checked
against the deposit's councillor names by the validator.

Supplemental files under `release/mumbai/` carry no `reservation` column and stay out of
the pooled machinery on purpose: `bmc_seats_2007.csv` (2007 winners with the
women's flag only; caste reservation unknown), `bmc_candidates_<year>.csv` for
1997, 2002, 2012 and 2017, and the Praja Foundation ward-by-wave citizen ratings
of councillors, `praja_ward_ratings_2011_2018.csv`, in which the satisfaction
item is inverted in the 2018 wave and flagged rather than repaired. The 1997 and
2002 councils have no reservation roster here, and rural Maharashtra's ~28,000
gram panchayats are absent entirely.

The next completed BMC general election was January 15, 2026; the expected
2022 election did not take place. `release/mumbai/bmc_winners_2026.csv` contains
all 227 winners and their final reservation categories (114 women-reserved).
The reservation parser checks category totals against the November 28, 2025
final gazette. Every vote count agrees with the January 19, 2026 official
gazette retained under `raw/mumbai/source_review/`; English names and party
labels come from OpenCity and have not received a separate row-by-row audit.
This winner-only supplement does not yet contain reservation, education, or
losing candidates. It does not establish a cross-election ward link.

See [the source review](source_review.md) for the 2012 correction, 2026 receipts,
and the scope of checks.

## Provenance

Every row carries `source_path` and `source_page` — the document it was read from and the page within it. The documents are committed here, so any row can be checked against the page it came from without a network round trip. That mattered repeatedly: nearly every parser bug in this repository produced plausible wrong values rather than an error, and opening the page was the only way to settle it.

All 3 cited documents are present.

Inventory for this directory: 10 tabular, 3 stata-do, 2 digital-text, 1 scan, 1 mixed, 1 bibtex, 35 pages total.

## Reproducing

```
make maharashtra
```

Parses from the committed documents and rewrites the files above, then runs `src/local_elections/states/maharashtra/validate.py`.

## What is checked

Every state runs a shared battery first — the seat key is unique, the reservation label agrees with the two fields it summarises, every `source_path` exists and every `source_page` falls inside its document. Then this state's own checks, which are the ones that catch silent corruption because they appeal to something outside the data:

- 227 seats in each council, one per ward
- the statutory women's share (one half from 2012) and the 27% Backward Class share
- the 2012 reservation against the deposit's independently digitised flag
- winner names against the deposit's councillors for 2012 and 2017

Column meanings are in [../../docs/dictionary.md](../../docs/dictionary.md). Expectation violations across every state are triaged into [../stats/expectations_report.csv](../stats/expectations_report.csv).
